actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 406 - 1 (Roll no. 119). (text: 5/5/2025 CR H1819-1820)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 406 - 1 (Roll no. 119). (text: 5/5/2025 CR H1819-1820)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H1894-1895)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 1503.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H1819)
Mr. Mast moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.

Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

activities.name: Bills of Interest - Exchange of Letters

dimensions.assessment: Affects individuals implicated in forced organ trafficking, foreign entities subject to sanctions, and convicted criminals facing passport restrictions.
dimensions.evidence: President shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a list of each person that... facilitates forced organ harvesting

dimensions.assessment: Imposes severe asset-blocking and visa-denial sanctions, and authorizes the denial or revocation of passports.
dimensions.evidence: block and prohibit all transactions in all property and interests in property... ineligible to receive a visa

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative enforcement costs for sanctions and reporting without specifying new funding amounts.
Adds reporting requirements to foreign assistance laws, grants passport-revocation authorities, and mandates executive branch sanctions.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of State may refuse to issue a passport to any individual who has been convicted of an offense

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory authorities for sanctions, reporting, and passport actions, with temporary 180-day waiver provisions.
dimensions.evidence: waive the application of sanctions... for periods not to exceed 180 days each

missing_information: Exact number of individuals or entities anticipated to be placed on the sanctions list
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates sanctions against individuals and entities involved in forced organ harvesting, requires annual foreign country reporting, and authorizes passport revocations for convicted offenders.
